newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to start probe into Clabecq aid.
newsitem.headline: EU to start probe into Clabecq aid.

text.p: The European Union will later this month open a formal inquiry into 1.5 billion Belgian francs of state aid programmed for ailing steel maker Forges de Clabecq SA, renewing the cloud of uncertainty over the company's future.
"We will probably open an inquiry at the end of September," a European Commission source told Reuters on Friday.

Belgian newspapers reported this week that loss making Clabecq had already received a 200 million franc bridging loan from its major shareholder -- the Walloon Regional Government -- and a second tranche would be released this month. The loan is designed to keep Clabecq afloat pending an EU ruling on the aid.

The opening of a formal state aid inquiry at the end of September would make it highly unlikely EU industry ministers -- who have the ultimate say on the legality of aid to steel companies -- could reach a decision on the Clabecq case in the Irish Presidency of the EU which ends in December.
EU steel state aid inquiries normally last several months and ministers are next due to gather on November 14.

Any delay would hit Clabecq's finances. The company had debt and other charges of around 70 million francs a month before the rescue plan was announced in June, although company officials were quoted on Friday as saying the losses were now limited.
Under the Walloon region's rescue plan, 700 of Clabecq's 2,200 employees would retire early. The Commission is also likely to insist on capacity cuts.

The Commission has received complaints about the Clabecq aid from the European Steel Federation, Eurofer, the British government and "a fair number of companies," EU Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said in July.
Van Miert has already said he has doubts about the legality of the Walloon region's plan.
